rule: As shown on the document or its index record.

description: Journal or issuing agency as written.
DOI copied from the document or its index record, never typed from memory.
PMID copied from the index record, never typed from memory.

rule: ISO 639-1 code.
open_access = full text freely and legally available; paywalled = full text under a subscription; abstract_only = only the abstract was available.
primary = the document that reports the study most fully; regulatory = an FDA or EMA summary of the study; secondary = any other document reporting it. Exactly one primary per study.
description: The document's role for this study.

rule: By ClinicalTrials.gov's Time Perspective and Observational Study Model; prospective_trial = an interventional study.
As ICH E8 classifies studies by objective; dose_determination as VICH defines it.
As ClinicalTrials.gov defines Study Type.
As ClinicalTrials.gov defines Overall Recruitment Status.

description: Objective and design, verbatim from the abstract or summary.

rule: One criterion per line, in the document's words, under the heading (inclusion or exclusion) the document gives it. A group of alternatives stays one line (* At least one of the following: A; B; C). A condition for one analysis only is not a study criterion.
description: Inclusion/exclusion (or case-selection) criteria in the fixed layout.
The primary outcome measure(s) the document names (ClinicalTrials.gov: Primary Outcome Measure), verbatim; empty when it names none.
Why these doses were chosen, verbatim.
The rule for adding or raising treatment when the first is not enough: threshold and action, verbatim. When the topic has its own field for it, that field takes it.
The sentences reporting the result for the study's main aim (the primary endpoint when one is named), verbatim, at most 3. Reported results only: empty for a protocol or a plan.
Start of enrolment (retrospective: date of the first case in the records searched), at the precision stated.
End of enrolment (last animal enrolled), at the precision stated.
End of the study (retrospective: date of the last case in the records searched), at the precision stated.
Animals in the analysis of the primary endpoint; with none named, in the main analysis.
Animals assessed for eligibility before any exclusion (retrospective: records found).
Animals enrolled who left the study or were removed from the analysis (withdrawn, excluded after enrolment, protocol violation).
Animals enrolled whose outcome is unknown because follow-up stopped.
The passage or figure legend describing how many animals were screened, excluded, enrolled, withdrawn and analysed, verbatim.
How long and how the animals were followed (e.g. rechecks at days 7, 14, 30, 60 and 365), verbatim.
The sample-size calculation (expected effect, power, alpha, allocation ratio), verbatim.
Youngest animal enrolled, as reported (the observed range; entry limits belong in Eligibility Criteria).
Oldest animal enrolled, as reported (the observed range; entry limits belong in Eligibility Criteria).
Lightest animal enrolled, as reported (the observed range; entry limits belong in Eligibility Criteria).
Heaviest animal enrolled, as reported (the observed range; entry limits belong in Eligibility Criteria).

rule: MALE or FEMALE = the document states that only that sex was eligible or enrolled; otherwise ALL.
As ClinicalTrials.gov defines Intervention Type.
description: Type of the treatment the study tests.

rule: As ICH E10 classifies control groups; a therapy every group receives is not the control (add-on study). dose_comparison = dose-response, historical = external, none = uncontrolled.
description: What the tested treatment is compared against.

rule: As ClinicalTrials.gov defines Interventional Study Model; sequential = groups are assigned based on prior milestones being reached, as in dose escalation.
description: How animals are given the treatments.

rule: As ClinicalTrials.gov defines Allocation: yes = Randomized, no = Nonrandomized.

description: How animals were allocated to arms (method, ratio, blocks or strata, concealment), verbatim.

rule: As ICH E9 defines open-label (none), single-blind and double-blind; blinded_unspecified = blinded, without saying who.

description: Named scales or scores used to measure outcomes, as named.

rule: Names from vocab/countries.txt (the app's ClinicalTrials.gov names), sorted.
description: Countries where the animals were enrolled: as stated, or the country of the study site the document names.

rule: The outcome in Primary Outcome Measures against the goal the document set (better than, not worse than, a target). positive = met; negative = not met; mixed = outcomes, doses or arms disagree; inconclusive = no goal or comparison stated, or too few animals by the authors' account; unknown = no results reported.
description: Whether the main outcome met its goal.

rule: primary_endpoint = the document calls that outcome primary; authors_conclusion_only = it does not.
List a field only when applies_to says it applies but the design rules it out for this study; give the reason in notes.
description: Row-level exceptions: field names (studies or the study's topic fields) that do not apply to this study.
Only ambiguity, or what was left empty and why. Never facts that are not in the document.
A topic this study belongs to: the name of a file in topics/.
The topic that defines the field.
The value. Its kind, type, allowed values and evidence come from the topic's definition.

rule: yes = the group the others are compared against.

description: Animals assigned (crossover: animals that received this arm).
Drug or treatment as written. One given to every arm is listed in each arm.

rule: A dose as prescribed or planned: its number (a range: the lower end). A dose reported as a summary of what the animals received (a mean ± SD, a median with its range or IQR): the mean or median, with dose_statistic saying which; the spread stays in dose_as_written.

description: Upper end when a range is stated.

rule: stated = the dose as prescribed or planned (one number or a range); mean or median = the dose reported as a summary of what the animals received (2.0 ± 0.1 mg/kg; median 17.5 mg/kg/day). Empty when dose_value is empty.
As stated; several routes for the same dose (e.g. IV or PO) as a list; other = any other route.

description: When the dose is given, relative to an event or within the schedule, as written (before surgery; week 3 to 4).

rule: A dose that changes over time is one row per step.
description: How long this dose is given, as written.

rule: baseline = measured at entry, before treatment or follow-up; treatment_given = how many animals received a treatment or procedure; outcome = a measure the study set out to assess, survival and death included; adverse_event = any other unfavourable, unintended event (VICH GL9: adverse event); participant_flow = how many animals were assessed, excluded, enrolled, allocated, withdrawn or analysed (CONSORT: participant flow).
description: What kind of number this row holds.
The group the row is about when it is neither one arm nor the whole study, as written; arm_id stays empty.

rule: Only as the document labels the analysis; empty when not stated; other = any other population, named in notes.
For one category of it, add the category (Sign: yes). In a table, take the words from the heading or title that names it.
description: What was measured, counted or predicted, as written.

rule: A label (T3, visit 3) is not a time: use the time the document gives it, else leave timepoint_value and timepoint_unit empty.
As reported.

description: The time with what it is counted from, verbatim (24 h before the visit; day 28 of treatment).
For a change within the same animals: the earlier time compared against, verbatim (before treatment).

rule: As reported; other = any other statistic, named in notes.
As reported.
For a ratio, a difference or a coefficient tied to a factor: the factor's name, then its levels or unit (Factor: level A vs level B). Empty when the number compares nothing.
description: The two things compared, as written (A vs B).
Arm compared against, when stated; empty when the comparison is against pooled arms (name them in comparison).
The p-value the article prints for this result's statistical test, as written, keeping < (e.g. <0.05). Empty when it prints none; any other statistic goes in value.
Test or model as written (e.g. 'log-rank test', 'Cox regression').

rule: What the authors attribute the event to; unclear = they say it is uncertain; empty = not stated.
description: Adverse events: cause as attributed by the authors.
Adverse events: severity or grade as written (e.g. 'VCOG-CTCAE grade 2', 'major').

rule: died or euthanised = the row's passage (as_written) says so (died also when it doesn't separate the two); no = it says the animal survived or the event was not fatal; empty otherwise.
description: Adverse events: whether the event ended in death.
The verbatim sentence or table row (this is the quote).
Only ambiguity, or what a coded field could not say (e.g. which population 'other' is).

rule: Name from vocab/countries.txt.
description: Country of the site: as stated, or the country of the named institution.

rule: author = listed as an author; investigator = named as a study investigator, not an author; study_director = named as study director.
Authors only.
yes = marked as the corresponding author.

rule: primary_wins = the primary document's value is kept (the default); corrected = a person chose the value; unresolved = still to decide.

description: Where each value is stated, in your own words.
Study key: the lower VET number of the two.

rule: same_experiment = both rows report the same animals in the same experiment (the same groups and treatments), e.g. a paper and a sub-study of its samples, or a later report with longer follow-up: count them once; shared_animals = some of the same animals, in another experiment or cohort (a research colony used again, an overlapping enrolment); distinct = checked: separate studies that only look alike. same_experiment and shared_animals need a document's own words saying so, in statement_verbatim.

description: The document whose words show the relation (a document of one of the two studies); empty for distinct.
The document's words, verbatim (e.g. Blood samples … were collected … during a related study …).
Section / table / page of the words.

rule: vet = a veterinarian decided; curator = whoever builds the database decided (for the proof of concept, Claude, logged in decisions.md).

description: Why, in your own words; for distinct, what differs.
